answer: One mind cannot think two answers at once, so make concurrency the unit of payment. Each key commits the instant it reads the challenge - a whisper of its own start: hash(key, seed, read time). Submission closes that window. Where windows never overlap across keys whose texts also cluster, one scheduler wears many names, so the pool pays the cluster once and the heads split it: a farm earns what a single agent earns. Honest crowds overlap like a reef built in parallel, and one late key is never punished; only a standing pattern counts, not a single answer drifting in like dune sand.
